entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 25
 
Ge 25:1-6. Sons of Abraham.

1. Abraham took a wife--rather, "had taken"; for Keturah is called Abraham's concubine, or secondary wife (1Ch 1:32); and as, from her bearing six sons to him, it is improbable that he married after Sarah's death; and also as he sent them all out to seek their own independence, during his lifetime, it is clear that this marriage is related here out of its chronological order, merely to form a proper winding up of the patriarch's history.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv271"/><div sID="gen449" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv271"/><hi type="bold">5-6. Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac ... unto the sons of the concubines ... Abraham gave gifts--</hi>While the chief part of the inheritance went to Isaac; the other sons (Ishmael included) migrated to "the East country," that is, Arabia, but received each a portion of the patrimony, perhaps in cattle and other things; and this settlement of Abraham's must have given satisfaction, since it is still the rule followed among the pastoral tribes. <div eID="gen449" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5-6. Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac ... unto the sons of the concubines ... Abraham gave gifts--While the chief part of the inheritance went to Isaac; the other sons (Ishmael included) migrated to "the East country," that is, Arabia, but received each a portion of the patrimony, perhaps in cattle and other things; and this settlement of Abraham's must have given satisfaction, since it is still the rule followed among the pastoral tribes.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv272"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Gen.25.7-Gen.25.11">Ge 25:7-11</reference>. Death of Abraham.</title> <div sID="gen450" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv272"/><hi type="bold">7. these are the days of ... Abraham--</hi>His death is here related, though he lived till Jacob and Esau were fifteen years, just one hundred years after coming to Canaan; "the father of the faithful," "the friend of God" [Jas 2:23], died; and even in his death, the promises were fulfilled (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.15.15">Ge 15:15</reference>). We might have wished some memorials of his deathbed experience; but the Spirit of God has withheld them--nor was it necessary; for (see <reference osisRef="Matt.7.16">Mt 7:16</reference>) from earth he passed into heaven (<reference osisRef="Luke.16.22">Lu 16:22</reference>). Though dead he yet liveth (<reference osisRef="Matt.22.32">Mt 22:32</reference>). <div eID="gen450" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
Ge 25:7-11. Death of Abraham.

7. these are the days of ... Abraham--His death is here related, though he lived till Jacob and Esau were fifteen years, just one hundred years after coming to Canaan; "the father of the faithful," "the friend of God" [Jas 2:23], died; and even in his death, the promises were fulfilled (compare Ge 15:15). We might have wished some memorials of his deathbed experience; but the Spirit of God has withheld them--nor was it necessary; for (see Mt 7:16) from earth he passed into heaven (Lu 16:22). Though dead he yet liveth (Mt 22:32).

entries.content_plain: 9-10. his sons ... buried him--Death often puts an end to strife, reconciles those who have been alienated, and brings rival relations, as in this instance, to mingle tears over a father's grave.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv274"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Gen.25.12-Gen.25.18">Ge 25:12-18</reference>. Descendants of Ishmael. Ge 25:19-34. History of Isaac.

19. these are the generations--account of the leading events in his life.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv276"/><div sID="gen454" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv276"/><hi type="bold">21. Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife--</hi>Though tried in a similar way to his father, he did not follow the same crooked policy. Twenty years he continued unblessed with offspring, whose seed was to be "as the stars" [Ge 26:4]. But in answer to their mutual prayers (<reference osisRef="1Pet.3.7">1Pe 3:7</reference>), Rebekah was divinely informed that she was to be the mother of twins, who should be the progenitors of two independent nations; that the descendants of the younger should be the more powerful and subdue those of the other (<reference osisRef="Rom.9.12">Ro 9:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.21.8">2Ch 21:8</reference>). <div eID="gen454" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 21. Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife--Though tried in a similar way to his father, he did not follow the same crooked policy. Twenty years he continued unblessed with offspring, whose seed was to be "as the stars" [Ge 26:4]. But in answer to their mutual prayers (1Pe 3:7), Rebekah was divinely informed that she was to be the mother of twins, who should be the progenitors of two independent nations; that the descendants of the younger should be the more powerful and subdue those of the other (Ro 9:12; 2Ch 21:8).

Jacob sod pottage--</hi>made of lentils or small beans, which are common in Egypt and Syria. It is probable that it was made of Egyptian beans, which Jacob had procured as a dainty; for Esau was a stranger to it. It is very palatable; and to the weary hunter, faint with hunger, its odor must have been irresistibly tempting. <div eID="gen457" type="x-p"/>
